questions.question: A passenger in a moving bus is thrown forward when the bus suddenly stops. This is explained

options.text: by the principle of conservation of momentum

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Newton's first law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Newton's laws of motion-

 
 
• **​Newton’s first law** states that, **if a body is at rest or moving at a constant speed in a straight line, it will remain at rest or keep moving in a straight line at constant speed unless it is acted upon by force.**

 
 
• **This postulate is known as the law of inertia**. The law of inertia was first formulated by Galileo Galilei for horizontal motion on Earth and was later generalized by René Descartes.
 
• Before Galileo, it had been thought that all horizontal motion required a direct cause. Still, Galileo deduced from his experiments that a body in motion would remain in motion unless a force (such as friction) caused it to come to rest.
 
 
 
• Newton’s second law is a quantitative description of the changes that **a force can produce in a body's motion**.
 
 
• It states that the time rate of change of a body's momentum is equal in both magnitude and direction to the force imposed on it.
 
• The momentum of a body is equal to the product of its mass and its velocity. Momentum, like velocity, is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction.
 
• A force applied to a body can change the magnitude of the momentum, direction, or both.
 
• For a body whose mass m is constant, it can be written in **F = ma**, where F (force) and an (acceleration) are vector quantities.
 
• If a body has a net force acting on it, it is accelerated by the equation. Conversely, if a body is not accelerated, there is no net force acting on it.
 
 
 
• Newton’s third law states that when two bodies interact, they apply forces to one another that are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.
 
• The third law is also known as the law of action and reaction. This law is important in analyzing static equilibrium problems, where all forces are balanced, but it also applies to bodies in uniform or accelerated motion.
 
• The forces it describes are real ones, not mere bookkeeping devices. For example, a book resting on a table applies a downward force equal to its weight on the table.
 
• **According to the third law, the table applies an equal and opposite force to the book.** This force occurs because the book's weight causes the table to deform slightly so that it pushes back on the book like a coiled spring.

questions.question: A certain sum is deposited for 4 years at a rate of 10% per annum on compound interest compounded annually. The difference between the interest at the end of 2 years and that at the end of 4 years is Rs. 5,082. Find the sum (in Rs.).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

We know, successive interest of a% and b% = [a + b + ab/100]%

The successive interest for 2 years = [10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100]% = 21%

The successive interest for 3 years = [21 + 10 + (21 × 10)/100]% = 33.1%

The successive interest for 4 years = [33.1 + 10 + (33.1 × 10)/100]% = 46.41%

The difference of interest between 4 and 2 years = 46.41 - 21 = 25.41%

So, 25.41% → 5082

Then, 100% → (5082/25.41) × 100 = 20000

∴ The sum (in Rs.) is Rs. 20000

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A certain sum is deposited for 4 years at a rate of 10% per annum on compound interest compounded annually.

Formula used:

At compound interest, the final amount = P(1+(r)/(100) )^n-P

Where, P = The sum of the amount

r = Rate of interest

n = Time (years)

**Calculation:**

Let, the sum of amount = x

[x(1+(10)/(100) )⁴-x]-[x(1+(10)/(100) )²-x] = 5082

⇒ [x((11)/(10) )⁴-x]-[x((11)/(10) )²-x] = 5082

⇒ (14641x)/(10000) - x - (121x)/(100) + x = 5082

⇒ 14641x/10000 - 121x/100 = 5082

⇒ 2541x/10000 = 5082

⇒ x = 5082 × (10000/2541) = 20000

**∴ The sum (in Rs.) is Rs. 20000**

questions.question: Two resistors, A (20 Ω) and B (40 Ω), are connected in parallel. The combination is connected to a 6 V battery. The currents in A and B are respectively ________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.3 A and 0.15 A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a **parallel circuit**, the voltage across each branch is the same; hence **VA=VB=6 V**.
 
• By **Ohm’s law** (*I = V/R*): IA = 6/20 = **0.30 A**, IB = 6/40 = **0.15 A** → matches option 3.
 
• Currents in parallel branches are **inversely proportional to resistances**; here IA/IB = RB/RA = 40/20 = 2, consistent with 0.30 A vs 0.15 A.
 
• Check: **Rₑq = (R₁R₂)/(R₁+R₂) = 13.33 Ω**, so total current = 6/13.33 ≈ 0.45 A = 0.30 + 0.15 A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm’s law forms**: V = IR, I = V/R, R = V/I—fundamental for branch-current calculations. 
 
• In parallel, the **total current equals the sum** of branch currents (Kirchhoff’s Current Law).
 
• **Equivalent resistance in parallel** is always less than the smallest branch; for two resistors use *product-over-sum*.
 
• **Power in a resistor**: P = VI = I²R = V²/R; at 6 V, PA=1.8 W and PB=0.9 W, so the lower resistance dissipates more power.

questions.question: If the areas of three adjacent faces of a cuboid are 5 cm², 15 cm², 27 cm², respectively, the surface area of the cuboid is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The areas of three adjacent faces of a cuboid are 5 cm², 15 cm², and 27 cm².

**Concept:**

The surface area of a cuboid is given by the formula:

Surface Area = 2(lw + lh + wh)

**Calculation:**

Let the dimensions of the cuboid be l, w, and h.

We have the following equations based on the areas of the faces:

⇒ lw = 5 cm² ......(1)

⇒ lh = 15 cm² ......(2)

⇒ wh = 27 cm² ......(3)

Multiplying all three equations, we get:

⇒ (lw) × (lh) × (wh) = 5 × 15 × 27

⇒ (lwh)² = 2025

⇒ lwh = √2025

⇒ lwh = 45

Now we can find each dimension using the equations (1), (2), and (3):

⇒ h = 45 / lw = 45 / 5 = 9 cm

⇒ w = 45 / lh = 45 / 15 = 3 cm

⇒ l = 45 / wh = 45 / 27 = 5/3 cm

Now, we calculate the surface area using these dimensions:

⇒ Surface Area = 2(lw + lh + wh)

⇒ Surface Area = 2(5 + 15 + 27)

⇒ Surface Area = 2(47)

⇒ Surface Area = 94 cm²

**∴ The surface area of the cuboid is 94 cm².**

Relative speed = (Speed of the train) - (Speed of the person)

Distance = Relative speed × Time

Distance travelled by the train relative to the person = 300 m (since the train crosses the person completely)

Relative speed = Distance / Time

⇒ Relative speed = 300 / 50 = 6 m/s

Now, Relative speed = Speed of the train - Speed of the person

⇒ 6 = Speed of the train - 3

⇒ Speed of the train = 6 + 3

⇒ Speed of the train = 9 m/s

**∴ The speed of the train is 9 m/s.**
